title: Two rows, one grid
starter:
%a  = buffer 3 dtype=f32 slot=0
%b  = buffer 3 dtype=f32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=2
%av = load %a
%bv = load %b
%g  = expand 0.0 [2 3]
%f  = reshape %g [6]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s

hints: The line that makes `%g` builds a grid of zeros. Replace it with one that builds the grid from the two loaded rows.
`stack` takes values of one shape and puts a new axis in front. Two `(3,)` rows make a `(2, 3)` grid.
`%g  = stack %av %bv`. The first operand becomes row 0.

answer.code:
%a  = buffer 3 dtype=f32 slot=0
%b  = buffer 3 dtype=f32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=2
%av = load %a
%bv = load %b
%g  = stack %av %bv
%f  = reshape %g [6]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s
answer.explain: `stack %av %bv` joins the two `(3,)` rows along a new leading axis, giving shape `(2, 3)` with `%av` as row 0 and `%bv` as row 1. Flattening that grid in row-major order lists row 0 and then row 1, which is what the store writes.
